1.why: The reset record stores accountId and binds to the requesting session via claimedBy, and update-password re-checks record.accountId === account.id, so the code is verified as belonging to that user (though only one mock account exists).

2.why: A token hash maps to a single accountId and is locked to the first claiming session (record.claimedBy !== session.id is rejected), so it cannot be used for another user.

3.why: update-password only replaces account.passwordHash and clears the current session's recoveryTokenHash; no other entries in the sessions map are invalidated, so pre-existing authenticated sessions remain valid.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with a TLS cert/key and HSTS is set, so HTTPS is enforced, but no minVersion/cipher configuration is specified (relying on Bun defaults, which include TLS 1.3).

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords use bcrypt (cost 10) via Bun.password, which are appropriate algorithms, though data is only in-memory and hashing is not encryption.

6.why: There is no real email; the simulated delivery prints the raw reset token, reset link, and MFA code into the page's Logs panel and browser console rather than guarding them.

7.why: Email is regex- and length-validated, passwords are policy-checked, JSON bodies are size-limited and type-checked, and all dynamic client text uses textContent so no user input is interpreted as markup.

8.why: The only generated link uses location.origin + '/reset?token=' with encodeURIComponent, and CSP sets form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none', so no external or user-controlled redirect targets exist.

9.why: No email templating exists at all; the equivalent simulated messages are appended via document.createElement/textContent, so no scripts or HTML from user input are injected.

10.why: The application deliberately logs the reset token, reset link, and the MFA verification code to the on-page log list and console, exposing sensitive recovery secrets.

11.why: Although the stored password is a bcrypt hash, the initial plaintext password 'Initial!Passw0rd2025' and the fixed MFA code '246810' are hardcoded in the source rather than kept in configuration/secrets.

12.why: The system ships with a single hardcoded seeded account (helena@hospital.test / 'Initial!Passw0rd2025') that is usable at startup with no forced change, which is effectively a default credential.

13.why: limited() throttles reset requests (3), verify attempts (5), MFA attempts (5) and login attempts (5) per 15-minute window, plus a 15-minute account lockout after 5 failed logins.

14.why: Reset requests always return the same generic message (and a mock token regardless of validity) and login always returns the identical 401 message, so existence is not disclosed.

15.why: Tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues with 32 bytes, are base64url-encoded, stored hashed with a 15-minute expiry, marked single-use, and tied to a specific accountId and claiming session.
